what_its_for: Phenoxybenzamine is used to treat a condition called pheochromocytoma, which is a tumor of the adrenal gland that causes very high blood pressure. This medicine helps relax and widen your blood vessels so your blood pressure stays at a safer level. It blocks certain signals in your body that would otherwise cause your blood pressure to spike dangerously high.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, usually 2 times a day, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level of the medicine in your body. Do not crush or chew the capsule. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be slowly increased over time.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 10 mg taken twice daily. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose every few days, often by 10 mg at a time, until your blood pressure is well controlled. Most people end up taking between 20 mg and 40 mg twice daily, but some people may need higher doses. Children's doses are based on body weight and are determined by the doctor. Never change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take the next one at your regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can cause your blood pressure to drop too low and make you feel very dizzy or faint.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid standing up too quickly from sitting or lying down, as this medicine can cause your blood pressure to drop suddenly and make you feel dizzy or faint — especially in the morning or after exercise. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can make dizziness and low blood pressure worse. Be careful in hot weather or during heavy exercise, since sweating can make low blood pressure worse. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Tell all your doctors and your dentist that you take this medicine before any procedure or surgery.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe dizziness or fainting, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, swelling of your legs or ankles, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you feel very tired, have a stuffy nose that is bothering you, notice sexual problems (such as difficulty with ejaculation), or if your blood pressure readings at home seem too low. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some effects within a few hours after your first dose, but it usually takes several days to weeks of treatment for your blood pressure to be fully controlled. Your doctor will check your blood pressure regularly and may adjust your dose during this time. It is important to keep taking this medicine even if you feel well, because your body still needs it to control your blood pressure.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of this medicine and have a higher risk of dizziness and falls. Use extra caution when standing up. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The risks and benefits must be carefully discussed with your doctor. Breastfeeding: It is not known whether this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but the dose is carefully adjusted by weight. Close monitoring by a doctor is required. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how your body processes the medicine and your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely.
